page: Microsoft Azure E64s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with symmetric multithreading enabled. The processing hardware consists of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.8 GHz, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI alongside hardware cryptographic features like AES and VAES. The configuration is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, with a zero GPU count, and there is no bundled local ephemeral storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and memory throughput. The multi-core profile achieves top-quartile performance across tests, registering 62,152.98 on stress-ng multi-core, 16,533.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 60,927.22 on PassMark CPU. High-capacity memory bandwidth reaches 296.85 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 136.92 GB/sec for writes. Database operations in PassMark reach 30,812.67, complemented by a throughput of 62.15 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Conversely, single-threaded execution remains in the median tier, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,674.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 1,899.89. Without dedicated GPU accelerators, large language model generation on 70B parameter models is limited to 2.73 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the absence of bundled local disks requires provisioning remote premium storage volumes for all disk operations, which should be factored into overall architectural cost calculations. However, the substantial 512 GB memory pool and robust multi-threaded processing density provide high efficiency for enterprise applications that demand persistent caching and low memory contention. The instance is suited for enterprise relational database management systems, in-memory data structures like Redis, distributed caching, software compilation, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64s_v5 is a memory-optimized server configuration featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 260 MB of L3 cache, the system incorporates AVX-512 vector instructions and cryptographic acceleration. It includes 512.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, but contains no local storage or GPUs. Synthetic benchmarks show strong multi-core processing with a Geekbench score of 16,533.0 and multi-threaded decompression at 300.56 GB/sec, while single-core processing remains average. Memory bandwidth is substantial, yielding 296.85 GB/sec on uncached reads and supporting 62.15 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance is suitable for large in-memory databases, Redis caches, high-concurrency enterprise applications, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.

tagline: Dedicated 64-vCPU architecture with 512 GB system memory designed for large-scale in-memory databases and multi-threaded enterprise processing.
